text: Name an ML model or tool named after an animal
note: Name is, or plainly is, an animal (mythical ones like Hydra, Pegasus count). Llama versions are one answer; branded derivatives (Code Llama) are separate

answers.q: The YAML-driven LLM fine-tuning toolkit, named for the salamander that stays a larva its whole life.
Yandex's gradient boosting library. The Cat is for categorical features, not the animal. We allow it.
DeepMind's 2022 generalist agent: one transformer playing Atari, captioning images and stacking blocks. Gato is Spanish for cat.
Named for Monty Python, not the snake, though the logo and the O'Reilly cover disagree. We allow it.
Gu & Dao's 2023 selective state-space model. The snake name nods to the hissing S's of SSM.
70B params on 1.4T tokens beat 280B Gopher. ~20 tokens per parameter became gospel.
Meta's open-weights family (Feb 2023). The first release was research-only; the weights hit 4chan within a week.
LLaMA 7B tuned on 52K self-instruct demos for under $600.
A LLaMA tuned on ShareGPT chats. Claimed '90% of ChatGPT quality', as judged by GPT-4.
Abu Dhabi's TII topped the Open LLM Leaderboard with it in 2023.
Named for 'panel data', not the bear. Wes McKinney started it at AQR Capital in 2008.
DeepMind's 280B model, promptly beaten by its smaller sibling Chinchilla.
A small model taught by imitating GPT-4's step-by-step explanations (Microsoft, 2023).
The QLoRA paper's model: a 65B fine-tune that fits on one 48GB GPU.
Named after the cloned sheep. Dolly 2.0 shipped with 15K human-written instructions.
Berkeley's 2023 LLaMA chat fine-tune. Databricks' Koalas was pandas-on-Spark, now inside PySpark.
DeepMind's 2022 few-shot VLM: a frozen Chinchilla plus gated cross-attention. OpenFlamingo is the open replica.
Found by program search, not a human (Google, 2023). Uses only the sign of the update, so it stores less than Adam.
Rust DataFrame library with a lazy query engine; the polar-bear challenger to pandas.
The Python data-science distribution, named for the snake as a wink at Python.
Waikato's Java ML workbench, named after a flightless New Zealand bird.

aka: Pre-training with Extracted Gap-sentences for Abstractive Summarization
answers.q: Google's 2019 abstractive summarizer, pretrained by masking whole 'gap sentences'.
Meta's config framework for ML experiments: compose YAML groups, override from the command line. Many heads, one run.
Georgi Gerganov's C/C++ inference engine: 4-bit LLaMA on a MacBook in March 2023, and the origin of GGUF.
The RAG framework formerly called GPT Index, renamed LlamaIndex in 2023.
Berkeley's LLM fine-tuned to write correct API calls; the team also runs the function-calling leaderboard.
The 2020 drop-in replacement for Iris: Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo penguins from the Palmer Archipelago.
Long convolutions plus gating as an attention replacement (2023). HyenaDNA read million-base genomes.
Eric Hartford's 'uncensored' fine-tunes, trained on an open recreation of Orca's data. An orca is a dolphin, so it fits.
LoRA fine-tunes of Llama 2 on the small, curated Open-Platypus STEM set. Topped the Open LLM Leaderboard in Aug 2023.
Berkeley's 7B chat model trained with RLAIF on the GPT-4-ranked Nectar dataset (2023).

aka: Communicative Agents for Mind Exploration of Large Language Model Society
answers.q: CAMEL (KAUST, 2023): two role-playing LLM agents, a user and an assistant, converse their way through a task.
Llama 2 trained further on code, with fill-in-the-middle (Aug 2023).
1.1B Llama-architecture model on 3T tokens: well over 100x the Chinchilla ratio.
The fast out-of-core online learner; the name is 'vorpal rabbit' as Elmer Fudd would say it.
Adobe's generative image model family (2023), trained on licensed Adobe Stock and public-domain content.
Yale's cross-domain text-to-SQL benchmark: 10,181 questions over 200 databases, with test databases never seen in training.
Two Otters: a PaLM 2 size, and a multimodal OpenFlamingo-based model tuned on the MIMIC-IT instruction set.
The smallest PaLM 2 size, small enough for a phone. Also Google's text-embedding model distilled from LLMs.
The second-largest PaLM 2 size, and the name behind text-bison and chat-bison on Vertex AI.
The largest PaLM 2 size in Google's report. Mythical, but we allow it.
NVIDIA's fast open ASR models in NeMo. Its sibling is Canary: two birds, one toolkit.
NVIDIA's multilingual speech recognition and translation model, a Parakeet sibling.
DeepMind's 2018 distributed RL agent: many actors, one learner, corrected by V-trace.
Meta's text-to-image and video models. BAAI's multimodal Emu shares the name.
James Betker's autoregressive-plus-diffusion TTS (2022). Slow by design, hence the name.
Apple's 2023 multimodal LLM that can refer to and ground any region of an image.
Faster, leaner LLM fine-tuning kernels. 'Un-sloth': the logo is a sloth.
A Python dataframe API that compiles to many SQL backends. Named for the wading bird.
DeepMind's 2024 mix of gated linear recurrences and local attention. RecurrentGemma is built on it.

aka: Layer-wise Adaptive Moments optimizer for Batch training
answers.q: Layer-wise Adaptive Moments for Batch training: trained BERT in 76 minutes with huge batches (You et al., 2019).
DeepMind's rule-following dialogue agent, built on Chinchilla (2022).
Meta's early-fusion model: text and image tokens in one stream (2024).
Nexa AI's Octopus v2: a 2B on-device model for function calling, using special 'functional tokens'.
Two Phoenixes: Arize's LLM observability and eval tool, and a 2023 multilingual ChatGPT-style LLM.
The recurrence-only sibling of Griffin in the same DeepMind paper (De et al., 2024).
RWKV-5 'Eagle', half of 'Eagle and Finch' (2024). NVIDIA also has a multimodal Eagle.
RWKV-6 'Finch', the other half of 'Eagle and Finch' (2024), with data-dependent decay.
RWKV-7 'Goose' (2025): the next RWKV after Eagle and Finch.
RWKV-Raven is the chat fine-tune of RWKV-4. NexusRaven is a separate function-calling LLM.
XLang Lab's open LLM balanced between text and code, built for language agents (2023).
AI2's 2021 T5-based question answerer that beat GPT-3 on some tests. Macaw-LLM is a separate image/audio/video model.
LLaMA-65B aligned from scratch by principle-driven self-alignment, with under 300 lines of human annotation.
Multilingual instruction-tuned LoRA adapters over 52 languages. A Bactrian is the two-humped camel.
Instruction-tuned LLMs with RLHF in 26 languages (2023).
From the RRHF paper: LLaMA taught to rank responses instead of running PPO (2023).
Open bilingual LLM family from Tiger Research, 7B to 180B (2023).
ImageBind plus Vicuna: an instruction follower that takes images, audio, video and more (2023).
Snap's 70M-clip video-caption dataset, captioned by an ensemble of cross-modality teacher models (CVPR 2024).
Google's open-vocabulary detector. OWL is for Open-World Localization; OWLv2 self-trains on web images.
Alibaba DAMO's modular multimodal LLM (2023), with v2 and v3 successors.
A 2023 multimodal LLM that writes bounding-box coordinates as plain text. A shikra is a small hawk.
CVPR 2021 best-paper compositional neural feature fields for scene generation. Also Abacus.AI's long-context Llama 2.
Meta's instruction-backtranslation model (2023): LLaMA writes the instructions for web text, then trains on them.
Math generalist models tuned on a hybrid of chain-of-thought and program-of-thought data (2023).
Stability AI's Orca-style Llama 2 fine-tunes, originally released as FreeWilly.
An SDXL fine-tune (2024) that took over anime and furry art. Its 'score_9' tags became a meme.
Prompt an aligned LLM with only its chat-template prefix and it writes the user instruction itself: free alignment data (2024).
An LLM writes Python that calls vision modules to answer visual questions (Columbia, 2023). A viper is a snake.
A learned linear attention that mimics softmax's spikiness, from 'The Hedgehog & the Porcupine' (2024).
The C++ linear algebra library underneath mlpack.
UCI regression staple: predict an abalone's age from physical measurements, shell rings and all.

aka: BIg Bench for LaRge-scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQL
answers.q: BIg Bench for LaRge-scale Database grounded text-to-SQL (2023): 12,751 pairs over 95 databases with dirty values.
CMU's open speech-recognition toolkit. Also SPHINX, a 2023 multimodal LLM from Shanghai AI Lab.

aka: Southeast Asian Languages In One Network
answers.q: Southeast Asian Languages In One Network. A fellow lion, respect.
Meta's Llama-based safety classifier for prompts and responses (2023).
Berkeley's permissively licensed reproduction of LLaMA, trained on RedPajama (2023).
Mozilla's single-file executable LLMs, built on llama.cpp (2023).
